title: Calibration orchestration for GPTQ/AWQ hybrid INT8 profiles and compatibility sweep
creator: Asha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Add a reproducible orchestration and CI/regression guard for integrating INT8 weight-only profiles produced by both GPTQ and AWQ toolchains, plus a compatibility sweep that validates binary/backwards compatibility across recent runtime changes. Scope includes profile ingestion, calibration snapshot playback, per-layer scale audits, and a canary pipeline that exercises the stack end-to-end (profile registry -> serving runtime -> evaluation harness).

Background: We have an increasing set of GPTQ/AWQ produced INT8 weight-only profiles. Past regressions have slipped through due to nondeterministic calibration seeds, sequence-length-aware behavior, and mixing profile variants in the registry. This ticket standardizes the calibration orchestration, introduces hybrid-profile compatibility checks (GPTQ vs AWQ parity and graceful fallback), and wires a smoke/regression job into CI that gates merges to runtime-1.22 affecting kernel selection and cache handling.

Deliverables:
- Orchestration playbook (automation + config) to run calibration snapshot playback for a given model/profile pair.
- A canary pipeline that generates golden metrics vs baseline (perplexity, exact-match on eval set, token-level logits drift, response sampling divergence) and emits pass/fail.
- Compatibility sweep harness that checks serving backwards compatibility for profile binary blobs and profile->runtime feature negotiation (seq-aware quant params).
- CI job entries and flakiness mitigations: retries, deterministic seeds, and golden-seed mode for nightlies.

Out-of-scope: FP8 end-to-end hardware validation (separate hardware team work), long-running A/B customer experiments (will hand off to PM once canary passes).
acceptance_criteria: Orchestration runs reproducibly (same metrics within noise band) when using golden-seed mode across 3 runs
Canary pipeline fails PRs that cause >1.5% drop in EM or >2.0% relative increase in token-level KL vs baseline for any model in the sweep
Compatibility sweep detects profile-schema mismatches and reports migration suggestions (e.g., missing per-head scaling) to a dashboard
CI job completes within 45 minutes on dedicated runner or marks as manual if resource unavailable
Documentation (Confluence) describing playback commands, env variables, and rollback procedure is published and linked in the ticket
tasks: Design orchestration config (YAML) for profile playback + env matrix (model sizes, seq lengths)
Implement profile registry ingestion test harness and binary validator
Hook up calibration snapshot playback tool and capture metrics artifacts (logits, tokens, per-layer scales)
Create canary CI workflow in .github/workflows/canary-quant.yml with gating thresholds
Add metric exporters and a lightweight dashboard tile for 'quant-regression' in Console (telemetry query)
Write rollback and fallback guidance: when to disable profile routing and how to revert to float or previous profile
notes: Decision: Use golden-seed deterministic mode for CI but keep stochastic replay for nightly drift detection.
Tradeoff: Full-sweep across all models would be expensive; initial sweep targets 6 representative checkpoints (llama-7b, llama-13b, mixtral-8x, mpt-30b, open-source-edu-3b, code-oriented model).
Observation: AWQ profiles show lower layer0 amplitude variance on validation set X; GPTQ tends to produce slightly more conservative scaling at attention heads.
Fallback strategy: Implement soft-routing in runtime to prefer exact-sequence-length-compatible profiles; if mismatch, revert to float or coarser-profile to preserve latency SLOs.

test_plan: 1) Run calibration playback in golden-seed mode for the six representative models. Collect per-layer scales, logits, tokens. 2) Compute EM, token-level KL, and sampling divergence vs baseline. 3) If any model crosses thresholds, fail canary and attach artifacts. 4) Run compatibility sweep: load every profile blob from registry and attempt pad/seq-negotiation in runtime; report schema mismatches. 5) Nightly: run full stochastic drift job at lower sampling to detect long-tail regressions.
